// This fixture is the shape internal/graph/propertytype.go really has, in
// miniature: an open string type, a second constant family declared in its
// own block, and the PropertyType table itself.
//
// It is the control. Every other fixture here differs from it in one stated
// way, so an error a row reports is attributable to that difference — and
// this one must produce no error at all, because the second block below is
// the reason PropertyTypes tolerates specs it cannot read a value off rather
// than refusing them everywhere.
//
// Nothing here is compiled. testdata is invisible to the go command, and
// go/parser does not type-check, so the fixtures that follow can hold shapes
// a compiler would refuse.
package graph

// PropertyType is the type whose constants the walk collects.
type PropertyType string

// PropertyTypeKind is a second constant family, and the one that makes the
// `read != 0` half of the walk's refusal load-bearing: every spec in its
// block is unreadable to this walk — the first is typed for another type,
// the rest inherit iota and carry neither a type nor a value — so a refusal
// that fired on unreadable specs alone would refuse the real source.
type PropertyTypeKind int

const (
	KindScalar PropertyTypeKind = iota
	KindList
)

const (
	TypeString PropertyType = "STRING"
	TypeBool   PropertyType = "BOOL"
)
